title: A single inference process underlies the behavior and neural circuits of working memory
abstract: arXiv:2611.22054v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Working memory holds past inputs online for future behavior. Despite decades of research, accounts of working memory remain divided across levels of analysis, with long-standing debates on whether its capacity reflects discrete slots or continuous resources, how attention improves recall, and whether its representations rely on persistent neural firing or activity-silent states. Here we show that MemGP, a theory that is specified at the computational, algorithmic, and circuit levels of analysis simultaneously, can explain diverse behavioral and neural phenomena in working memory. At the computational level, MemGP casts working memory as probabilistic inference over a continuous function on feature space, with a variational objective that balances memory strength against a Gaussian-process prior. At the algorithmic level, writing, storing, and reading of memories correspond to approximating this posterior with a finite set of inducing p

translated_title: 一个统一的推理过程支撑着工作记忆的行为与神经环路
translated_abstract: 工作记忆将过去的输入在线保持以供未来行为使用。尽管经过数十年的研究，关于工作记忆的解释仍然分散在不同的分析层面之间，并存在长期争论：其容量究竟反映离散的“槽位”还是连续的“资源”、注意如何改善回忆、以及其表征依赖持续神经放电还是“活动静默”状态。在此，我们展示了一个同时在计算、算法和神经环路三个分析层面上明确规定的理论——MemGP——能够解释工作记忆中多样的行为与神经现象。在计算层面，MemGP 将工作记忆视为对特征空间上一个连续函数的概率推断，其变分目标在记忆强度与高斯过程先验之间取得平衡。在算法层面，记忆的写入、存储和读取对应于用一组有限的诱导点来近似该后验分布。
tldr: 该论文提出 MemGP 理论，将工作记忆统一为对特征空间连续函数的概率推断过程，从而在计算、算法和神经环路三个层面同时解释了工作记忆的多种行为与神经现象。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MemGP, a theory unifying working memory as probabilistic inference over a continuous function in feature space, which explains diverse behavioral and neural phenomena simultaneously at the computational, algorithmic, and circuit levels.
